newsitem.title: FINLAND: Kemira board gets issue authorisation.
newsitem.headline: Kemira board gets issue authorisation.

text.p: An extraordinary shareholders' meeting of Finnish chemicals group Kemira Oy on Wednesday authorised the company's board to issue up to eight million new shares, Kemira said in a statement.
The authorisation is in force until the next scheduled annual general meeting -- May 30, 1997 at the latest, Kemira said -- but it gave no details of any planned issue.
Kemira announced on September 10 it was seeking approval to issue up to eight million new shares. At the same time, the government announced it planned to sell some of its Kemira shares this year.

The board has the right to raise the share capital in one or more tranches at subscription terms set by the board, Kemira said. It was also authorised to diverge from existing shareholders' privileges to subscribe to new shares.
Kemira currently has 120.8 million shares with a nominal value of 10.00 markka each.
The state owns 72.3 percent of shares and is authorised by parliament to lower the holding to 50.1 percent, Kemira said.
The government said it planned to lower the state's ownership to "around 55 percent taking into account any new shares to be included in the offering by Kemira."
Kemira said on Wednesday the funds raised would be used to expand its core business activities through acquisitions or other investments.
